review_notes: Read the whole file and compared the Gram eigenbasis proofs with CourantFischer.lean and Sylvester/Internal/SpectralBounds.lean. The only strong repetition is the eigenbasis-expansion argument in the two extreme-singular-value gain bounds. Other repeated pieces were too short to report. Those are the `comp_apply`/`adjoint_inner_left`/`inner_self_eq_norm_sq` rewrite, the sqrt-of-square step in the two `exists_norm_apply_eq_...` theorems, and the `norm_adjoint_apply_le` calc. I did not check whether importing SpectralBounds into this file would create an import cycle, so I propose a private lemma local to this file or one added to CourantFischer.lean. The proposed rewrites are sketches and have not been compiled.

findings.excerpt: have hpars : ∑ i : Fin n, ‖(hsym.eigenvectorBasis hn).repr x i‖ ^ 2 = ‖x‖ ^ 2 := by
findings.problem: The two gain bounds repeat the same argument. Each expands `re ⟪(A⋆A) x, x⟫` in the Gram eigenbasis, and each re-proves Parseval (`hpars`) with an identical `simp_rw [repr_apply_apply]; exact sum_sq_norm_inner_right` block. Each then runs a `Finset.sum_le_sum` with `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right ... (sq_nonneg _)`, using a pointwise eigenvalue bound from `eigenvalues_antitone`. The only difference is the direction of the comparison and the constant (`λ_{n-1}` versus `λ_0`). The same mathematics is a third and fourth time in this repo: `re_inner_le_of_eigenvalues_le` / `le_re_inner_of_le_eigenvalues` in SpectralBounds.lean (specialised to `hn = rfl`), and the span-restricted lemmas in CourantFischer.lean. Each copy re-derives Parseval, so the file carries long inline calc chains where a one-line application of a lemma would do.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a general-`hn` pair of lemmas, either private in this file or in CourantFischer.lean next to `re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq`. For `hT : T.IsSymmetric`, `hn : finrank 𝕜 E = n` and `c : ℝ`:
`re_inner_le_of_forall_eigenvalues_le (hc : ∀ i, hT.eigenvalues hn i ≤ c) (x) : RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜 ≤ c * ‖x‖ ^ 2`, and the dual `le_re_inner_of_forall_le_eigenvalues (hc : ∀ i, c ≤ hT.eigenvalues hn i) (x) : c * ‖x‖ ^ 2 ≤ RCLike.re ⟪T x, x⟫_𝕜`.
Proof sketch: rewrite with `re_inner_apply_self_eq_sum_eigenvalues_mul_sq`, bound termwise with `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hc i) (sq_nonneg _)`, and close with `← Finset.mul_sum` and the existing Parseval step (`sum_sq_norm_inner_right` after `repr_apply_apply`).
Then in `singularValues_last_mul_norm_le` the `hsq` block becomes `rw [sq_norm_apply_eq_re_inner_gram, mul_pow, A.sq_singularValues_of_lt hn hlast]; exact le_re_inner_of_forall_le_eigenvalues hsym hn (fun i => hsym.eigenvalues_antitone hn (Fin.le_def.mpr (by omega))) x`.
In `norm_apply_le_singularValues_zero_mul` it becomes `rw [sq_norm_apply_eq_re_inner_gram, mul_pow, A.sq_singularValues_of_lt hn hn0]; exact re_inner_le_of_forall_eigenvalues_le hsym hn (fun i => hsym.eigenvalues_antitone hn (Fin.le_def.mpr (Nat.zero_le _))) x`.
The SpectralBounds.lean lemmas could then be restated as the `hn = rfl` special case, subject to the import order.
findings.benefit: Removes about 40 lines of duplicated calc and Parseval reasoning from this file. The two extreme-singular-value proofs then show only their real content, the monotonicity of the eigenvalues. A single maintained statement replaces four copies of the quadratic-form eigenvalue bound across the repo.
